hlni.insight: A task label alone does not reveal assessment demands; you must decompose the product, criteria, and feedback separately.
hlni.audienceGap: Students assume degree titles represent the specific nature of course assessments.
hlni.viewerChange: Students will shift from guessing based on labels to asking for explicit assessment criteria.
hlni.support: The method isolates three distinct components of academic assessment, preventing assumptions about degree content.
hlni.payoff: The method turns an ambiguous task into a concrete, unanswered question that the student can use to vet a course.

reelTitle: B.Com vs BBA: Beyond the Labels
creativeAngle: Applying the Assessment Decomposition Method to evaluate degree tasks
objective: Teach students how to objectively compare academic tasks to make informed decisions
targetAudience: +2 students seeking academic depth and well-supported course and career decisions

shots.name: The Vague Task
shots.visual: A student looks confused at a tablet screen displaying a course description.
shots.dialogue: Choosing between B.Com and BBA based on titles? That is a guessing game.
shots.onscreenText: Task: Analyze the quarterly report and present findings.

shots.name: The Decomposition Grid
shots.visual: Split screen. Left: Task description. Right: A three-column grid being filled in: Product, Criteria, Feedback.
shots.dialogue: Try this: decompose the task. What is the product? What is the criterion? What feedback is available?

shots.name: The Concrete Question
shots.visual: The student points at the empty 'Criteria' column on the grid.
shots.dialogue: Unanswered cells are your clues. What specific criterion determines a successful analysis versus a presentation?
shots.onscreenText: Ask: What is the specific criterion?

productionNotes.camera: Steady, tripod-mounted shots with clear close-ups of the grid
productionNotes.editing: Direct cuts between the student and the grid graphics
productionNotes.sound: Clear voiceover with no background music
productionNotes.casting: A relatable student in a casual environment

creativeSummary.keyCreativeIdea: Use a three-column decomposition method to force clarity when comparing academic degree tasks.
shootingPriority: The student identifying the missing criteria

selected.title: The Assessment Decomposition Method
selected.audienceGap: Students assume degree titles reveal assessment methods, leading to misaligned expectations.
selected.hlni: A task label alone does not tell you what you must produce, what will be assessed, or what feedback you receive. Ask these as separate questions.
selected.viewerChange: Shift from guessing based on degree titles to asking for specific task criteria.
selected.concept: A professional breakdown of a sample task showing how to isolate the product, the criteria, and the feedback.
selected.device: A split-screen view: one side shows a vague task, the other shows the three-column audit grid.
selected.support: The method separates three different pieces of information; it does not assume particular course content.
methodSteps: Ask what criterion is used to assess it.
Ask what feedback is available; mark unknown answers as questions.
selected.interpretationRule: Use the unanswered cells to ask a precise question about the actual course or task before deciding.
selected.visibleProof: A three-column question sheet turns one vague preference into a concrete unanswered question.
selected.payoff: Use the unanswered cells to ask a precise question about the actual course or task before deciding.
selected.limitations: This is a question-forming aid, not a degree ranking, aptitude test or prediction of success.

demonstration.input: A sample task description for a business course module.
demonstration.visibleInput: Task: Analyze the quarterly report and present findings.
demonstration.observation: The student identifies that 'analyze' and 'present' are two distinct assessment demands.
demonstration.nextQuestion: What specific criterion determines a successful analysis versus a presentation?
